This guide shows how to validate an Excel submission from your own R package.

It uses the survey files and `total_count` callback from [Authoring validation rules](rules-authoring.html).

## 1. Add dependencies and resources

Declare `form.model`, `form.references` and `form.validation` in your package's `Imports`.

Store the survey files and callback in these locations:

```text
inst/forms/
  survey-form.yaml
  references.yaml
  survey-validation.yaml
  survey-structure-validation.yaml
  survey-generated-validation.yaml
  survey-business-validation.yaml
R/
  checks.R
```

## 2. Load the form model and references

Replace `your.package` with your package name and configure catalogue sources and lookups together in `references.yaml`.

```r
# Locate the installed form definitions and validation files.
validation_directory <- system.file("forms", package = "your.package")
# Load the survey form model.
form_model_definition <- form.model::load_form_model("survey", validation_directory)
# Read the lookup settings shipped with the consumer package.
reference_configuration <- form.references::read_reference_configuration(
  file.path(validation_directory, "references.yaml"))
# Retrieve the tables required by the form model using the deployment source configuration.
reference_preparation <- form.references::prepare_model_references(
  form_model_definition, reference_configuration)
```

Preparation retains catalogue file paths and checksums for evidence reports.

## 3. Load the validation plan

Register the callback defined in `R/checks.R`:

```r
# Prepare validation from the resolved form model, leaving the original definition unchanged.
validation_plan <- form.validation::read_validation_plan(
  file.path(validation_directory, "survey-validation.yaml"), reference_preparation$model,
  checks = list(total_count = total_count))
```

You can reuse this plan for submissions using the same form and rules.

## 4. Validate a submission

```r
# Read the submitted form while preserving Excel cell positions.
submission_data <- form.validation::read_workbook_data("submission.xlsx")
# Execute validation using the prepared rules and reference values.
validation_result <- form.validation::validate_data(
  validation_plan, submission_data, reference_preparation$references, source = "submission.xlsx"
)
```

Inspect the findings and check whether the submission passed:

```r
# Display the validation findings.
validation_result$findings
# Accept only a completed validation with no errors.
validation_accepted <- validation_result$complete && isTRUE(validation_result$valid)
```

Use the [report guide](validation-reports.html) to generate HTML and CSV output from this result.

## Optional: convert values before content checks

If your application accepts values such as numeric text or textual booleans, use this validation call instead:

```r
# Execute validation using the prepared rules and reference values.
validation_result <- form.validation::validate_data(
  validation_plan, data, reference_values, source = "submission.xlsx",
  prepare_data = function(data) {
    form.validation::prepare_validation_data(data, validation_plan$model)
  }
)
```

Preparation runs after structural checks pass and uses the types declared in the form model.

Supported values are converted; invalid values remain available for validation to report.
